LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_FIVE.lessonTitleEnglish: What Job Do You Want to Do?
LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_FIVE.learnerPromise: Say what happens during a situation or moment.
LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_FIVE.explanation: Put the event or situation before 的時候. Then say what happens inside that moment.

lessonWorld.title: Open a moment at the bakery
lessonWorld.prompt: Guoan will ask the boss when he sees him tomorrow.
lessonWorld.traditional: 我看到老闆的時候，幫你問他。
lessonWorld.simplified: 我看到老板的时候，帮你问他。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Wǒ kàndào lǎobǎn de shíhou, bāng nǐ wèn tā.
lessonWorld.english: When I see the boss, I will ask him for you.

teachingGlossary.meaning: done; shows a change or finished action
links an action to how it went

patternRows.english: Chat while eating.
Listen to music when unhappy.
Drink water while exercising.

items.question: When working, I use Chinese — is it 工作時候 or 工作的時候?
items.answer: Keep 的. 的 connects the situation to 時候: 工作的時候.

right.english: When working, speak Chinese.

items.question: When I feel unhappy, I listen to music. Where does 不好 go?
items.answer: Keep the situation together: 心情不好, then 的時候. 的時候 needs the whole situation before it.

right.traditional: 心情不好的時候，聽音樂。
right.simplified: 心情不好的时候，听音乐。
right.pinyin: Xīnqíng bù hǎo de shíhou, tīng yīnyuè.
right.english: When I feel unhappy, I listen to music.

items.question: I drink water while exercising. Is 運動以後 okay?
items.answer: No. 運動以後 means after exercising. For inside the moment, use 運動的時候.

right.pinyin: Yùndòng de shíhou, wǒ hē shuǐ.
right.english: When exercising, I drink water.

liveSceneLab.title: Open a different life moment
liveSceneLab.description: The moment changes; 的時候 keeps the situation attached to what happens inside it.

choices.label: Eating
choices.subject: 我
choices.traditional: 吃飯的時候，我不用手機。
choices.simplified: 吃饭的时候，我不用手机。
choices.pinyin: Chīfàn de shíhou, wǒ bú yòng shǒujī.
choices.english: When eating, I do not use my phone.
choices.note: 吃飯 names the moment.

choices.label: Feeling down
choices.subject: 我
choices.traditional: 心情不好的時候，我會聽音樂。
choices.simplified: 心情不好的时候，我会听音乐。
choices.pinyin: Xīnqíng bù hǎo de shíhou, wǒ huì tīng yīnyuè.
choices.english: When I feel unhappy, I listen to music.
choices.note: A state can open the moment window.

choices.label: At work
choices.subject: 我
choices.traditional: 工作的時候，我常常說中文。
choices.simplified: 工作的时候，我常常说中文。
choices.pinyin: Gōngzuò de shíhou, wǒ chángcháng shuō Zhōngwén.
choices.english: When working, I often speak Chinese.
choices.note: 工作 is the situation.

liveSceneLab.takeaway: Name the moment first: situation + 的時候. Then say what happens.

examples.teachingNote: A weather situation opens the moment.

text.traditional: 天氣好的時候，我喜歡出去運動。
text.simplified: 天气好的时候，我喜欢出去运动。
text.pinyin: Tiānqì hǎo de shíhou, wǒ xǐhuān chūqù yùndòng.
text.english: When the weather is good, I like exercising outside.

examples.teachingNote: A routine rule inside a moment.

text.traditional: 在我們家，吃飯的時候，不可以用手機。
text.simplified: 在我们家，吃饭的时候，不可以用手机。
text.pinyin: Zài wǒmen jiā, chīfàn de shíhou, bù kěyǐ yòng shǒujī.
text.english: In our home, do not use a phone while eating.

examples.teachingNote: A complete action can name the moment.

text.traditional: 他玩電腦的時候，都不跟別人說話。
text.simplified: 他玩电脑的时候，都不跟别人说话。
text.pinyin: Tā wán diànnǎo de shíhou, dōu bù gēn biérén shuōhuà.
text.english: When he uses the computer, he does not talk to others.

examples.teachingNote: A feeling can name the moment.

text.traditional: 我心情不好的時候，都會聽音樂、跟朋友聊天。
text.simplified: 我心情不好的时候，都会听音乐、跟朋友聊天。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xīnqíng bù hǎo de shíhou, dōu huì tīng yīnyuè, gēn péngyǒu liáotiān.
text.english: When I feel unhappy, I listen to music and chat with friends.

LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_FIVE.exercisePreview: Attach 的時候 to the situation.

questions.correctFeedback: 的 connects the situation to 時候.
The complete situation comes before 的時候.

LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_FOUR.lessonTitleEnglish: What Job Do You Want to Do?
LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_FOUR.titleTraditional: 在經驗履歷上蓋一個過
LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_FOUR.titleEnglish: Mark a Life Experience with 過
LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_FOUR.learnerPromise: Talk about past experiences with 過 and state completed actions with 過了.
LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_FOUR.explanation: Use 過 after an action word to talk about life experience—something you have ever done before. When paired with 了 at the end, it means you already did it today, so you don’t need to do it again.

lessonWorld.title: Open Zhongming’s work history
lessonWorld.prompt: Zhongming has worked in a restaurant before.
lessonWorld.pinyin: Wǒ yǐqián zài cāntīng shàngguo bān.
lessonWorld.english: I have worked in a restaurant before.

teachingGlossary.meaning: done; shows a change or finished action
links an action to how it went

LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_FOUR.pattern: 經驗：V + 過 ｜ 完成：V + 過 + 了

patternRows.english: I have seen this movie before.
Many Taiwanese people have been to Japan.
I have already eaten breakfast.
She has already been here.

items.question: Have you ever tried stinky tofu — 吃了 or 吃過?
items.answer: 吃過. 了 asks about one finished meal. 過 asks whether it ever happened in your life.

right.english: Have you ever tried stinky tofu?

items.question: I have worked at a restaurant. Where does 過 go?
items.answer: Between the two parts of 上班: 上過班. It cannot sit at the end of the whole action.

right.english: I have worked at a restaurant before.

items.question: I have not been to Japan — 不 or 沒 before 去過?
items.answer: 沒. 沒 says the experience never happened. 不 says you refuse or will not do it.

right.english: I have not been to Japan.

discoveryLab.title: Event or life experience?
discoveryLab.description: Both forms can be correct. Choose the viewpoint the question needs.

choices.label: Last year
choices.english: I went to Japan last year.
choices.note: 了 reports a particular trip in a dated story.

choices.label: Ever before
choices.english: I have been to Japan before.
choices.note: 過 adds Japan to the speaker’s life experience.

choices.label: Tried it?
choices.english: Have you ever tried stinky tofu?
choices.note: No exact date is needed; the question asks about experience.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Particular event? Use the event form. Ever in your experience? Use 過.

text.traditional: 很多台灣人去過日本，因為從台灣到日本不遠。
text.simplified: 很多台湾人去过日本，因为从台湾到日本不远。
text.pinyin: Hěnduō Táiwānrén qùguo Rìběn, yīnwèi cóng Táiwān dào Rìběn bù yuǎn.
text.english: Many Taiwanese have been to Japan, because it is not far from Taiwan to Japan.

text.traditional: A: 他來過我們家嗎？ B: 來過，那個時候你不在家。
text.simplified: A: 他来过我们家吗？ B: 来过，那个时候你不在家。
text.pinyin: A: Tā láiguo wǒmen jiā ma? B: Láiguo, nàge shíhou nǐ bù zài jiā.
text.english: A: Has he ever been to our home? B: Yes, he came; you weren't home at that time.

text.traditional: A: 你吃過臭豆腐嗎？ B: 我還沒吃過，聽說很特別。
text.simplified: A: 你吃过臭豆腐吗？ B: 我还没吃过，听说很特别。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ chīguo chòudòufu ma? B: Wǒ hái méi chīguo, tīngshuō hěn tèbié.
text.english: A: Have you eaten stinky tofu? B: I haven't tried it yet; I hear it is unique.

text.traditional: A: 你要跟我們一起吃午飯嗎？ B: 我吃過了，你們去吃吧！
text.simplified: A: 你要跟我们一起吃午饭吗？ B: 我吃过了，你们去吃吧！
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ yào gēn wǒmen yìqǐ chī wǔfàn ma? B: Wǒ chīguo le, nǐmen qù chī ba!
text.english: A: Do you want to eat lunch with us? B: I've already eaten; you all go ahead!

text.traditional: A: 李小姐今天要來我們公司，她來過了嗎？ B: 她來過了，是早上來的。
text.simplified: A: 李小姐今天要来我们公司，她来过了吗？ B: 她来过了，是早上来的。
text.pinyin: A: Lǐ xiǎojiě jīntiān yào lái wǒmen gōngsī, tā láiguo le ma? B: Tā láiguo le, shì zǎoshang lái de.
text.english: A: Miss Li is visiting our company today; has she already come? B: She has already been here; she came in the morning.

text.traditional: A: 他給大家寫了一張卡片，你們都看過了嗎？ B: 我看過了。 C: 我還沒看。
text.simplified: A: 他给大家写了一张卡片，你们都看过了吗？ B: 我看过了。 C: 我还没看。
text.pinyin: A: Tā gěi dàjiā xiě le yì zhāng kǎpiàn, nǐmen dōu kànguo le ma? B: Wǒ kànguo le. C: Wǒ hái méi kàn.
text.english: A: He wrote a card for everyone, have you all read it yet? B: I have already read it. C: I haven't read it yet.

LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_FOUR.exercisePreview: Decide whether the situation asks about one event or life experience.

segments.hint: Use verb + 過 for life experience.

questions.correctFeedback: 過 marks an experiential past action.
The question asks whether you have ever tried it before.
上過班 marks previous work experience.

questions.sectionLabel: Part 2 · Already Done for Now (過...了)

segments.traditional: 你要跟我們一起吃午飯嗎？我

segments.hint: Use V + 過了 to indicate you already ate.

questions.correctFeedback: 吃過了 indicates the meal was completed and does not need repeating.

questions.sectionLabel: Part 2 · Already Done for Now (過...了)

segments.traditional: 李小姐今天要來我們公司，她

segments.hint: Ask whether she has already visited.

questions.correctFeedback: 來過了嗎 asks if the scheduled visit already occurred.

questions.sectionLabel: Part 2 · Already Done for Now (過...了)

segments.hint: Ask whether they have already read it.

questions.correctFeedback: 看過了嗎 checks completion before the present moment.

subsections.title: Life Experience (Ever Done with 過)
subsections.explanation: Put 過 right after the action word to share something you have experienced at least once in your life, like “I have been to Japan.” Say 沒...過 for things you have never done.

patternRows.english: I have seen this movie.
Many Taiwanese people have been to Japan.

subsections.title: Already Done for Now (過 ... 了)
subsections.explanation: Use 過 with 了 at the end when an action was already completed earlier today and doesn’t need to be repeated, like “I already ate breakfast” or “I’ve already read the note.”

patternRows.english: I have eaten breakfast.
She has already been here.

LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_ONE.lessonTitleEnglish: What Job Do You Want to Do?
LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_ONE.learnerPromise: Say which language, device, or tool you use for an action.
LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_ONE.explanation: Put 用 before the tool, language, or method. Say the action after it.

lessonWorld.title: Meet Yiwen, the future reporter
lessonWorld.prompt: Yiwen wants a job where she can use two languages.
lessonWorld.traditional: 我希望用中文和英文工作。
lessonWorld.simplified: 我希望用中文和英文工作。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Wǒ xīwàng yòng Zhōngwén hé Yīngwén gōngzuò.
lessonWorld.english: I hope to use Chinese and English at work.

teachingGlossary.meaning: done; shows a change or finished action
links an action to how it went

patternRows.english: I write letters using Chinese.
I take photos using my phone.
He writes characters with a brush.

items.question: I write letters using Chinese. Where does 中文 go?
items.answer: 中文 is the tool, so it goes right after 用, before the action: 用中文寫信.

right.english: I write letters using Chinese.

items.question: Can you write with a brush — do I still need 用?
items.answer: Yes. 用 stays between 會 and the tool: 會用毛筆寫字. English drops the word “use”; Chinese does not.

right.pinyin: Nǐ huì yòng máobǐ xiě zì ma?
right.english: Can you write characters with a brush?

items.question: I chat with friends in Chinese — 用 or 跟 before 中文?
items.answer: 用. 用 names the language or tool. 跟 is for the person you do it with: 跟朋友.

right.pinyin: Wǒ yòng Zhōngwén gēn péngyǒu liáotiān.
right.english: I chat with friends in Chinese.

discoveryLab.title: Put the tool in the hand
discoveryLab.description: Change the tool and the same action gains a new method.

choices.label: Chinese
choices.english: I write letters using Chinese.
choices.note: 中文 is the language used.

choices.label: Phone
choices.english: I take photos with my phone.
choices.note: 手機 is the device used.

choices.label: Brush
choices.english: I write characters with a brush.
choices.note: 毛筆 is the physical tool.

choices.label: Repair the order
choices.traditional: 我用寫中文信 → 我用中文寫信
choices.simplified: 我用写中文信 → 我用中文写信
choices.pinyin: wǒ yòng xiě Zhōngwén xìn → wǒ yòng Zhōngwén xiě xìn
choices.english: Move the tool before the action.
choices.note: 用 + tool comes before what you do with it.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Tool first, action second: 用 + tool + action.

text.traditional: 我喜歡用中文寫信。
text.simplified: 我喜欢用中文写信。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuān yòng Zhōngwén xiě xìn.
text.english: I like writing letters in Chinese.

text.traditional: 他們常常用學校的網路上網。
text.simplified: 他们常常用学校的网络上网。
text.pinyin: Tāmen chángcháng yòng xuéxiào de wǎnglù shàngwǎng.
text.english: They often use the school internet to go online.

examples.teachingNote: A physical tool inside an ability question.

text.traditional: 你會用毛筆寫字嗎？
text.simplified: 你会用毛笔写字吗？
text.pinyin: Nǐ huì yòng máobǐ xiě zì ma?
text.english: Can you write characters with a brush?

text.traditional: 最近我常常用中文跟朋友聊天。
text.simplified: 最近我常常用中文跟朋友聊天。
text.pinyin: Zuìjìn wǒ chángcháng yòng Zhōngwén gēn péngyǒu liáotiān.
text.english: Recently I often chat with friends in Chinese.

segments.hint: Build 用 + 中文 + 寫信.

questions.correctFeedback: 中文 is the tool; 寫信 is the action.
questions.repairFeedback: Build 用 + 中文 + 寫信.

毛筆 appears before the action it enables.

LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_THREE.lessonTitleEnglish: What Job Do You Want to Do?
LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_THREE.titleTraditional: 看懂態度和影響的方向
LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_THREE.titleEnglish: Show an Attitude or Effect with 對
LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_THREE.learnerPromise: Use 對 to indicate who you speak to, what something affects, and how someone is treated.
LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_THREE.explanation: 對 points toward someone or something. Use it to speak toward someone, to say something is good or bad for your health, or to describe how someone treats others.

lessonWorld.title: Meet Guoan’s coworkers
lessonWorld.prompt: Guoan enjoys the bakery because his coworkers treat him well.
lessonWorld.pinyin: Tóngshì dōu duì wǒ hěn hǎo.
lessonWorld.english: My coworkers are all very kind to me.

teachingGlossary.meaning: done; shows a change or finished action
links an action to how it went

LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_THREE.pattern: 對人說話 ｜ 影響與益處 ｜ 對待態度

patternRows.english: I am telling this only to you; do not tell anyone else.
Using a phone often is bad for the eyes.
The boss treats us very well.

items.question: The boss is kind to me. Why does 我 come so early?
items.answer: 對 points at the receiver, so 我 follows it right away: 對我好. English puts “to me” at the end; Chinese does not.

right.english: The boss is kind to me.

items.question: My coworkers are kind to me. Did I say it right with 我對同事很好?
items.answer: No — you turned the arrow around. The person right after 對 receives the kindness, so it is 同事對我很好.

right.english: My coworkers are kind to me.

items.question: Phones are bad for my eyes — 對 or 跟 before 眼睛?
items.answer: 對. 對 shows where the effect lands. 跟 is for doing something together with someone.

right.english: Phones are bad for the eyes.

discoveryLab.title: Reverse the arrow, reverse the meaning
discoveryLab.description: Both directions can be grammatical. The arrow tells you who affects whom.

choices.label: Boss → me
choices.english: The boss is kind to me.
choices.note: I receive the boss’s kindness.

choices.label: Me → boss
choices.english: I am kind to the boss.
choices.note: The boss receives my kindness.

choices.label: Phone → eyes
choices.pinyin: Cháng yòng shǒujī duì yǎnjing bù hǎo.
choices.english: Frequent phone use is bad for the eyes.
choices.note: 眼睛 receives the negative effect.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Read the arrow: source → 對 → receiver → attitude or effect.

text.traditional: 他常對我說：「我們應該要多運動、多喝水。」
text.simplified: 他常对我说：「我们应该要多运动、多喝水。」
text.pinyin: Tā cháng duì wǒ shuō: "Wǒmen yīnggāi yào duō yùndòng, duō hē shuǐ."
text.english: He often says to me: "We should exercise more and drink more water."

text.traditional: 這件事我只對你說，你不要告訴別人。
text.simplified: 这件事我只对你说，你不要告诉别人。
text.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì wǒ zhǐ duì nǐ shuō, nǐ bú yào gàosù biérén.
text.english: I am telling this only to you; please do not tell anyone else.

text.traditional: 常用手機對眼睛不好。
text.simplified: 常用手机对眼睛不好。
text.pinyin: Cháng yòng shǒujī duì yǎnjīng bù hǎo.
text.english: Using a mobile phone often is bad for your eyes.

text.traditional: 這本書對我不難，我可以學學看。
text.simplified: 这本书对我不难，我可以学学看。
text.pinyin: Zhè běn shū duì wǒ bù nán, wǒ kěyǐ xuéxue kàn.
text.english: This book is not difficult for me; I can try to learn it.

text.traditional: 他對我很好，常常幫我的忙。
text.simplified: 他对很好，常常帮我的忙。
text.pinyin: Tā duì wǒ hěn hǎo, chángcháng bāng wǒ de máng.
text.english: He treats me very well and often helps me.

text.traditional: A: 老闆對你們怎麼樣？ B: 他對我們很不錯，常常要我們多注意身體健康。
text.simplified: A: 老板对你们怎么样？ B: 他对我们很不错，常常要我们多注意身体健康。
text.pinyin: A: Lǎobǎn duì nǐmen zěnmeyàng? B: Tā duì wǒmen hěn búcuò, chángcháng yào wǒmen duō zhùyì shēntǐ jiànkāng.
text.english: A: How does the boss treat you? B: He treats us very well, often telling us to pay attention to our health.

LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_THREE.exercisePreview: Choose the person or thing receiving the attitude or effect.

segments.hint: Use 對 + person + 說 to indicate speaking to someone.

questions.correctFeedback: 對我說 indicates the listener.
只對你說 indicates speaking exclusively to the listener.

questions.sectionLabel: Part 2 · Good or Bad for Something (對)

segments.hint: Use 對 + target + 不好 to express harmful effect.

questions.correctFeedback: 對眼睛不好 shows negative effect on health.

questions.sectionLabel: Part 2 · Good or Bad for Something (對)
questions.correctFeedback: 對我不難 indicates how difficult the subject is relative to the speaker.
對我們很不錯 shows a kind attitude toward the employees.
對我很好 expresses generous and friendly treatment.

subsections.title: Speaking to Someone (對 + Person + 說)
subsections.explanation: Put 對 before the person you are speaking to, like “he often says to me” (他常對我說).

patternRows.english: He often says to me: should exercise more.

subsections.title: Good or Bad for Something (對 + Body / Thing + 好 / 不好)
subsections.explanation: Say what is affected after 對, like “looking at phones often is bad for your eyes” (對眼睛不好).

patternRows.english: Using a phone often is bad for the eyes.

subsections.title: Treating Someone Well or Kindly (對 + Person + 很好)
subsections.explanation: Describe how someone treats people around them, like “the boss is very nice to us” (老闆對我們很不錯).

patternRows.english: The boss treats us very well.

LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_TWO.lessonTitleEnglish: What Job Do You Want to Do?
LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_TWO.titleTraditional: 把以前和以後放在正確的時間上
LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_TWO.titleEnglish: Place 以前 and 以後 on the Timeline
LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_TWO.learnerPromise: Use 以前 and 以後 as standalone time words, after specific times, and after action statements.
LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_TWO.explanation: 以前 means “before” or “in the past”; 以後 means “after” or “in the future.” You can use them on their own, or put them right after a time or an activity.

lessonWorld.title: Meet Zhongming’s past and future
lessonWorld.prompt: Zhongming’s old plan and future plan are different.
lessonWorld.traditional: 我以前想當老闆，現在想當醫生。
lessonWorld.simplified: 我以前想当老板，现在想当医生。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Wǒ yǐqián xiǎng dāng lǎobǎn, xiànzài xiǎng dāng yīshēng.
lessonWorld.english: I previously wanted to be a boss; now I want to be a doctor.

teachingGlossary.meaning: done; shows a change or finished action
links an action to how it went

LESSON_TWELVE_GRAMMAR_TWO.pattern: 獨立時間詞 ｜ 時間點＋以前／以後 ｜ 句子＋以前／以後

items.question: My coworkers are kind to me. Did I say it right with 我對同事很好?

items.question: Phones are bad for my eyes — 對 or 跟 before 眼睛?
items.answer: 對. 對 shows where the effect lands. 跟 is for doing something together with someone.

items.question: Have you ever tried stinky tofu — 吃了 or 吃過?
items.answer: 吃過. 了 asks about one finished meal. 過 asks whether it ever happened in your life.

right.english: Have you ever tried stinky tofu?

items.question: I have worked at a restaurant. Where does 過 go?
items.answer: Between the two parts of 上班: 上過班. It cannot sit at the end of the whole action.

right.english: I have worked at a restaurant before.

items.question: I have not been to Japan — 不 or 沒 before 去過?
items.answer: 沒. 沒 says the experience never happened. 不 says you refuse or will not do it.

right.english: I have not been to Japan.

discoveryLab.title: Event or life experience?
discoveryLab.description: Both forms can be correct. Choose the viewpoint the question needs.

choices.label: Last year
choices.english: I went to Japan last year.
choices.note: 了 reports a particular trip in a dated story.

choices.label: Ever before
choices.english: I have been to Japan before.
choices.note: 過 adds Japan to the speaker’s life experience.

choices.label: Tried it?
choices.english: Have you ever tried stinky tofu?
choices.note: No exact date is needed; the question asks about experience.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Particular event? Use the event form. Ever in your experience? Use 過.

text.traditional: A: 他來過我們家嗎？ B: 來過，那個時候你不在家。
text.simplified: A: 他来过我们家吗？ B: 来过，那个时候你不在家。
text.pinyin: A: Tā láiguo wǒmen jiā ma? B: Láiguo, nàge shíhou nǐ bù zài jiā.
text.english: A: Has he ever been to our home? B: Yes, he came; you weren't home at that time.

text.traditional: A: 你吃過臭豆腐嗎？ B: 我還沒吃過，聽說很特別。
text.simplified: A: 你吃过臭豆腐吗？ B: 我还没吃过，听说很特别。

text.traditional: A: 你要跟我們一起吃午飯嗎？ B: 我吃過了，你們去吃吧！
text.simplified: A: 你要跟我们一起吃午饭吗？ B: 我吃过了，你们去吃吧！
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ yào gēn wǒmen yìqǐ chī wǔfàn ma? B: Wǒ chīguo le, nǐmen qù chī ba!
text.english: A: Do you want to eat lunch with us? B: I've already eaten; you all go ahead!

text.traditional: A: 李小姐今天要來我們公司，她來過了嗎？ B: 她來過了，是早上來的。

text.pinyin: A: Lǐ xiǎojiě jīntiān yào lái wǒmen gōngsī, tā láiguo le ma? B: Tā láiguo le, shì zǎoshang lái de.
text.english: A: Miss Li is visiting our company today; has she already come? B: She has already been here; she came in the morning.

text.traditional: A: 他給大家寫了一張卡片，你們都看過了嗎？ B: 我看過了。 C: 我還沒看。
text.simplified: A: 他给大家写了一张卡片，你们都看过了吗？ B: 我看过了。 C: 我还没看。
text.pinyin: A: Tā gěi dàjiā xiě le yì zhāng kǎpiàn, nǐmen dōu kànguo le ma? B: Wǒ kànguo le. C: Wǒ hái méi kàn.

text.traditional: 國安，你每天下課以後都要去麵包店工作，辛苦嗎？
text.simplified: 国安，你每天下课以后都要去面包店工作，辛苦吗？
text.pinyin: Guó’ān, nǐ měitiān xiàkè yǐhòu dōu yào qù miànbāodiàn gōngzuò, xīnkǔ ma?
text.english: Guoan, you work at the bakery everyday after school. Is it tiring?

text.traditional: 不辛苦。我很喜歡這個工作，因為可以學怎麼做麵包，而且同事也都對我很好。
text.simplified: 不辛苦。我很喜欢这个工作，因为可以学怎么做面包，而且同事也都对我很好。
text.pinyin: Bù xīnkǔ. Wǒ hěn xǐhuān zhège gōngzuò, yīnwèi kěyǐ xué zěnme zuò miànbāo, érqiě tóngshì yě dōu duì wǒ hěn hǎo.
text.english: It’s okay. I like this job very much because I get to learn how to make bread. Moreover, the colleagues are very nice to me as well.

text.traditional: 這樣你在學校的成績，不會有問題嗎？
text.simplified: 这样你在学校的成绩，不会有问题吗？
text.pinyin: Zhèyàng nǐ zài xuéxiào de chéngjì, bú huì yǒu wèntí ma?
text.english: Does it affect your studies?

text.traditional: 不會啊！我都先做功課，再去工作。
text.simplified: 不会啊！我都先做功课，再去工作。
text.pinyin: Bú huì a! Wǒ dōu xiān zuò gōngkè, zài qù gōngzuò.
text.english: No, it doesn’t. I always do my homework first, and then go to work.

text.english: I have worked at a restaurant before. I was exhausted, and always didn’t get enough sleep.

text.english: Is it okay to work two hours? Does your bakery still need employees?

text.english: I don’t know. When I see my boss tomorrow, I’ll ask him about that for you.
